# Prologue: The Scars of the First Age

> *"The world did not die when the sky caught fire. It merely held its breath, waiting in the frozen dark until the stones themselves learned how to speak."*
> — *Book of Aurtus, The Second Chronicle*

When the old world ended, it did not go gently.

Humanity’s First Age choked on ash, radiation, and the shattering of tectonic plates. In those final, desperate years before the sky turned black, the architect engineers of the ARC Project buried the remnants of civilization beneath miles of granite and basalt. Deep within subterranean stasis crypts, thousands of souls were sealed into cryo-pods, programmed to sleep until the planetary atmosphere healed and the surface became hospitable once more.

They were meant to wake together. They were meant to rebuild a technological paradise.

They awoke to a nightmare.

Over centuries of dormancy, the earth did not heal in the manner the ancient scientists had predicted. Deep within the fractured mantle, alien mineral formations—towering crystals of obsidian, sapphire, and radiant emerald—sprouted like malignant forests across mountain ranges and desolate plains. The crystals did not merely glow; they bled energy. They warped the fundamental laws of physics, bleeding an exotic quantum resonance into the soil, the water, and the air.

This was the Source.

When the sleepers finally began to awaken, their pods did not open in unison. Clock cycles failed; geothermal circuits degraded; tectonic shifts crushed entire vaults. Sleepers tumbled out into the blinding daylight scattered across centuries. Those who emerged into the Second Age found an untamed, feudal frontier populated by the descendants of surface survivors and the ancient, arboreal Silvan clans.

And the crystals changed them.

Those born near the crystal fissures found themselves attuned to the energy. They could manipulate heat, density, and kinetic force with a thought. They became the Gifted—Source Mages. Around this strange new power arose the Church of Aurtus, a monastic order built upon the Four Tenets: Life, Order, Balance, and Memory. To safeguard the realm from rogue mages, the Order of the Wardens was established—elite adjudicators armed with rune-forged blades who traveled the frontiers dispensing justice and keeping the delicate peace between human settlements and the wild lands.

Yet the greatest threat to the Second Age did not come from the wild. It came from the East.

Decades before the others, an ARC sleeper of immense intellect and terrifying ambition had awakened in the eastern wastes. Where others saw the crystals as sacred or perilous, she saw them as raw material for absolute dominion. Imbuing her own biology with black crystal resonance, she declared herself Empress—the Black Queen.

From her towering obsidian citadel, the Empress built an empire of iron and flesh. Her alchemists harvested the blue crystal resin, forging terrifying cannons that spat liquid fire capable of vaporizing stone battlements. Her flesh-weavers bred twisted abominations—the Chimera—hybrid beasts engineered for battlefield slaughter. And at her right hand stood Lord Seer Juric Rogan, a zealot who enforced her will with cold, telekinetic brutality.

Then, Captain Marcus Gavin awoke.

Crash-landing in the rugged northern frontier, Marcus emerged from his pod with no memory of his past, carrying only the instinct of a soldier and the raw, uncorrupted genetics of the First Age. Taken in by Orah, a gentle farm woman in a secluded mountain valley, Marcus struggled to comprehend this brutal, beautiful new world. But peace was a luxury the Second Age could not afford.

The Empress’s scouts detected the energy signature of Marcus’s crash. Realizing that an uncorrupted ARC survivor carried the genetic key to unlocking ancient military vaults and mastering Source synthesis, the Empress dispatched Chancellor Rogan and her vanguard to hunt him down.

The clash at the mountain outpost was swift and devastating. The Empress’s resin cannons pulverized the old defenses. Though the Wardens—led by the fierce Lorin Corliss and Grand Adjudicator Uri—fought valiantly to protect the frontier, the outpost fell. Corliss and the surviving Wardens were forced to retreat toward the Barrens, while Marcus was driven into the wilderness with a spectral companion, hunted by an empire that would stop at nothing to claim his blood.

Now, the drums of war echo across the continent. 

In the high halls of the eastern capital, Lord Seer Rogan ascends the throne of judgment, ready to crush all who dare defy the Empress. In the shadowed keeps of the Church, the fanatic inquisitors of the Sword of the Faithful sharpen their silver blades. And in the deep woods of Silvan, Marcus Gavin must decide whether to keep running from his destiny... or stand and break the Black Queen's throne.


---
